main_dirt.bias_notes: Standard 1-mile dirt oval with a 905-foot home straight. The surface is highly reactive to local climate cycles, frequently turning deep, wet, and attritional. While early speed ('E') controls short sprints, the generous stretch allows mid-pack stalkers ('P') and closing swoopers ('S') an exceptionally fair shot in two-turn route races when the early tempo is hot.
main_dirt.post_bias: In dirt sprints (4.5f, 5f, and 6f), inside-to-middle draws (stalls 1-5) are strongly preferred to establish early tracking position. In dirt routes, the draw is largely neutral.

main_turf.bias_notes: Tight inner turf circuit with acute turns and a very short 700-foot straightaway. Demands high tactical agility and elite rail-skimming execution. Front-runners and box-seat pressers completely control the running lines, while deep closing styles face near-impossible traffic hurdles.
main_turf.post_bias: Inside posts (stalls 1-4) hold an overwhelming structural edge. Outside draws (8+) in turf routes face a severe penalty due to a minimal run-up before entering the first turn.

handicapping_angles.regional_shipper_class_drop: Mountaineer regularly draws horses shipping in from tougher Midwest circuits (Thistledown, Mahoning Valley, Presque Isle Downs, Parx). Heavily upgrade class-dropping shippers entering local MNR allowance or claiming fields.
handicapping_angles.wet_weather_slogging_filter: When rain hits the Ohio River Valley, the main dirt track turns into a deep, holding swamp. Prioritize verified mudlarks with strong wet-track speed figures, and fade pure fast-track front-runners whose scores compress under testing conditions.
handicapping_angles.turf_outside_draw_fade: On the turf course, aggressively downgrade 'Need-the-Lead' front-runners drawn in wide stalls (8+). They are forced to burn excessive energy crossing over before the tight first bend, leaving them highly vulnerable late.
handicapping_angles.wv_night_racing_variance: Mountaineer operates predominantly as a night racing venue. Watch for horses transitioning from afternoon racing to night racing under the lights, giving a slight edge to locally stabled runners with documented track familiarity.
